title: What is spooking markets as stocks, Treasury yields and gold all fall ahead of European trading?
summary: It looks like Halloween is coming a day early for markets with investors getting quite the fright already as we look to wrap up the trading week. Both stocks and Treasury yields are falling together, with gold also struggling to catch a bid. That's a rather spooky combination to deal with. So, what exactly is driving markets into this scary situation? Well, the latest earnings from Amazon overnight have only added another skeleton to the closet after the company's massive AI spending bill overshadowed impressive cloud growth. Amazon shares are down 7% in after-hours trading, and that follows from the beating that tech shares took yesterday after Alphabet reignited fears of AI spending in the day before. US futures are being dragged sharply lower today, with Nasdaq futures down 1.8% currently. And that is setting up a rather ominous backdrop ahead of European trading today. But beyond the selling in tech, there's something else about the broader market moves worth noting. Why are Treasury yields continuing to fall when inflation risks remain elevated? And why exactly aren't lower yields doing much to offer support for tech stocks? Perhaps the answer lies in the darker story brewing beneath the AI boom . For all the excitement surrounding AI technology, investors are starting to question just how much money companies need to throw at it before seeing meaningful returns. title: (Some good news!) Treasuries rally as AI selloff drives flight to safety, 10-year yield at one-month low
summary: Lower Treasury yields ease financing costs across the curve, offering some relief to rate-sensitive sectors and to the AI firms whose borrowing has worried investors. That makes the bond rally partly self-correcting for the very stress that triggered it. A softer dollar supports Asian currencies and commodities priced in dollars. Oil remains the main threat to the rally: with Brent heading for a fourth straight monthly gain, any escalation in the Iran conflict could quickly revive inflation fears and push yields back up. The BoJ decision later today is the next test, and a hawkish surprise could firm the yen against a softer dollar. --- Oil is higher: Vessel on fire in Strait of Hormuz after incident near Oman, cause "unknown" (LOL) Stocks slammed: Earnings bloodbath: Intel crashes over 22%, Amazon over 12%. title: Japan September factory output beats forecasts, but retail sales disappoint ahead of BoJ
summary: The data give the BoJ evidence on both sides, so the reaction in the yen and Japanese government bonds is likely to be modest ahead of the policy decision and Outlook Report later in the day. Stronger output and upbeat production plans support Japanese industrials and exporters. Softer retail sales could weigh on consumer-facing stocks if the weakness persists. The production upgrade suggests manufacturers are looking through high energy costs for now, but further gains in oil prices tied to the Iran conflict would squeeze margins and household spending power at the same time. --- Earlier: Tokyo October CPI 2.8% (2.7% expected) Still to come: BoJ preview: hold at 1.25% expected, with 2% inflation call and dissent risk in focus --- Japan’s factories are firing up while its shoppers are holding back, leaving the BoJ with one more mixed signal on a crowded morning.
